subject.title: Manual context clearing for tool results

question: Should OpenClaw add caller-directed per-tool-result lifecycle control, and if so should the canonical operation be destructive clear or recoverable archive/recover?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the permanent behavior changes session state, transcript integrity, replay, and agent authority, so implementation should not proceed before maintainers choose the lifecycle contract.

options.title: Recoverable archive contract
options.body: Add one canonical operation that removes selected tool results from active model context while retaining a recoverable/auditable reference for replay and later use.

options.title: Destructive clear contract
options.body: Allow explicit deletion or placeholder rewriting of selected tool results, accepting that some workflows may need to refetch lost state.

options.title: No new core API
options.body: Keep relying on pruning, truncation, compaction, reset, and delete, and close or defer manual lifecycle control as out of scope.

recommendation.title: Recoverable archive contract
recommendation.body: Add one canonical operation that removes selected tool results from active model context while retaining a recoverable/auditable reference for replay and later use.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter authored the cache-TTL pruning workaround and is the strongest current routing candidate for choosing whether core should grow this lifecycle surface.
